sections.t: The desert warthog is a stockily built animal growing to an average length of 125 centimetres (49 in) and weight of 75 kilograms (165 lb), with males being larger than females. It has a rather flattened head with distinctive facial paired protuberances ("warts") and large curving canine teeth that protrude as tusks. These are not present in juveniles, but grow over the course of a few years. They are larger in males than in females.

Desert warthogs live in social groups called "sounders", consisting mostly of females and their offspring, while males tend to live in solitude or form bachelor groups. A sounder occupies a home range of about 10 square kilometres (3.9 sq mi), which is usually centred on a water hole. The warthogs dig a number of burrows, or take over holes excavated by other animals, and move from one to another.

The desert warthog is native to the Horn of Africa. Its current range extends from southeastern Ethiopia through western Somalia to eastern and central Kenya. The subspecies P. a. aethiopicus, commonly known as the Cape warthog, once occurred in the southeastern parts of Cape Province and the adjacent parts of Natal Province, but became extinct around 1871.
